questions.question: Q1. What does the term 'reptation' mean in the context of 4D printing?

answers.a: The rapid cooling of the polymer as it exits the nozzle.
answers.b: The slithering motion of polymer chains across the interface between two roads as they weld.
answers.c: The springback motion observed during shape-memory actuation.
answers.d: The random vibration of the print head during extrusion.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Cooling happens after extrusion; it is separate from bonding.
explanations.b: Correct — Reptation describes chain diffusion across interfaces, the actual welding mechanism.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Springback is a 4D shape-memory response, not a printing mechanism.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Vibration causes dimensional variation, not inter-layer bonding.

questions.question: Q2. Which material property is set by the dwell time in the T_g–T_m crystallisation window?

answers.a: The crystallinity X_c and hence the stiffness E.
answers.b: The healing degree D_b at the weld.

explanations.a: Correct — Longer dwell in the growth window raises crystallinity, which stiffens the part.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Healing degree comes from reptation time, not crystallisation window.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Nozzle temperature is a user-set control, not set by dwell.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Bed temperature is a control input, not derived from dwell time.

questions.question: Q3. What does a high healing degree D_b (≥ 0.80) mean for the part's behaviour?

answers.a: The part will have higher crystallinity.
answers.b: The part will experience larger residual warpage.
answers.c: The part behaves isotropically; layers bond strongly and do not fail across the build direction.

explanations.a: Incorrect — D_b governs bonding, not crystallinity.
explanations.b: Incorrect — High D_b means strong bonds, which reduces warping from delamination.
explanations.c: Correct — Once D_b ≥ 0.80, the weld is strong enough that isotropic behaviour emerges.
explanations.d: Incorrect — D_b affects stiffness and geometry, not actuation speed.

questions.question: Q4. When cooling a printed road from extrusion temperature to room temperature, what changes in residual stress?

answers.a: Stress is zero until the part reaches T_g, then rises suddenly.
answers.b: Stress accumulates continuously due to constrained thermal contraction from the bed and layers below.
answers.c: Stress appears only after the part is fully cooled and removed from the bed.
answers.d: Stress in 4D parts is entirely released by the shape-memory network.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Stress builds gradually as thermal mismatch accumulates throughout cooling.
explanations.b: Correct — The blocked shrinkage converts to locked-in residual stress during the entire cool-down.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Stress forms while the part is still on the bed, during the thermal gradient.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The shape-memory network can actuate, but it does not erase residual stress.

questions.question: Q5. In the Tsai-Hill criterion for off-axis strength, why does the weakest plane occur near 45–55° rather than at 90°?

answers.a: The nozzle passes at a diagonal angle and causes directional wear.
answers.b: The FDM process always creates a preferred 45° fibre orientation.
answers.c: Crystallinity is lowest in the diagonal direction.
answers.d: The shear term in the criterion drives a minimum between the along-road and cross-road directions.

explanations.a: Incorrect — The nozzle path does not cause the shear weakness.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Raster angle is user-controlled; the weakness is a mechanical consequence, not a default.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Crystallinity is uniform; orientation of existing roads sets the anisotropy.
explanations.d: Correct — The Tsai-Hill formula includes a shear-stress term (1/τ_LT²) that dominates near 45–55°.

questions.question: Q6. The anisotropy ratio AR for PLA is approximately 47/24 MPa. What does this number represent?

answers.a: The ratio of along-road strength (σ_L) to cross-road strength (σ_T).
answers.b: The ratio of print temperature to bed temperature.
answers.c: The ratio of crystallinity to amorphous fraction.
answers.d: The ratio of cooling time to reptation time.

explanations.a: Correct — AR = σ_L/σ_T quantifies how much stronger the part is along the roads.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Temperatures do not enter the anisotropy ratio definition.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Crystallinity is measured as X_c, not via strength ratio.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Time constants are independent of the material strength anisotropy.

questions.question: Q7. In tolerance stack-up analysis, what is the key difference between root-sum-square (RSS) and worst-case (WC)?

answers.a: WC accounts for temperature drift; RSS ignores it.
answers.b: RSS is used for single features; WC is used for stacked features.
answers.c: RSS assumes all errors are independent and adds them in quadrature; WC assumes all errors align and adds them linearly.
answers.d: RSS is the current industry standard; WC is obsolete.

explanations.a: Incorrect — Both methods can include thermal errors; the difference is in how they combine.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Both methods apply to stacks; RSS is optimistic, WC is conservative.
explanations.c: Correct — RSS treats errors as uncorrelated; WC is the pessimistic bound when all errors reinforce.
explanations.d: Incorrect — WC remains the safety-critical bound; RSS is used alongside it for planning.

questions.question: Q8. The process-capability index C_pk targets a value of ≥ 1.33. What does this threshold mean?

answers.a: The mean of the process sits 1.33 standard deviations from the specification limit.
answers.b: The part shrinkage will not exceed 1.33% of the feature size.
answers.c: The process is centred with enough margin that even a 1σ shift still keeps 99.9% inside the band.
answers.d: There are at most 1.33 parts per million outside tolerance over the long run.

explanations.a: Incorrect — C_pk compares the margin to *three* standard deviations.
explanations.b: Incorrect — C_pk is unitless and applies to any tolerance band, not just shrinkage.
explanations.c: Incorrect — C_pk ≥ 1.33 provides some margin but not full immunity to drift.
explanations.d: Correct — A C_pk of 1.33 means the process margin is 4σ, yielding roughly 64 ppm defects (DPMO), acceptable for precision.

questions.question: Q9. A heated bed (60 °C) reduces warpage compared to an unheated bed. Why?

answers.a: A hot bed cools the part faster and reduces residual stress.
answers.b: The relaxation factor f_relax increases, allowing some residual stress to dissipate as the part cools near T_g.
answers.c: A heated bed prevents crystallisation, so the part remains flexible.
answers.d: The raster angle is automatically adjusted to reduce shear stress.

explanations.a: Incorrect — A hot bed slows cooling and increases dwell in the crystallisation window.
explanations.b: Correct — Near T_g the polymer chains have mobility; a warmer bed lets them relax some stress before stiffening.
explanations.c: Incorrect — A heated bed actually increases dwell time and can increase crystallinity.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Raster angle is a user input, not bed-temperature dependent.

questions.question: Q10. The cooling time constant τ_cool depends on road diameter d. If you halve d, what happens to τ_cool and therefore to the crystallinity X_c?

answers.a: τ_cool halves, dwell time t_x falls, and X_c decreases; the part becomes less stiff but a better actuator.
answers.b: τ_cool doubles, dwell time t_x rises, and X_c increases; the part stiffens and is a poorer actuator.
answers.c: τ_cool is unchanged because cooling is governed by the chamber, not the road size.
answers.d: τ_cool halves, but X_c stays constant because crystallinity is set by the polymer grade alone.

explanations.a: Correct — τ_cool = ρ·d·C_p/(4·h_conv) scales with d; smaller roads cool faster, shrinking the growth window and lowering crystallinity.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Halving d *decreases* τ_cool, shortening the crystallisation window.
explanations.c: Incorrect — The road diameter directly enters the cooling time constant.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Crystallinity is set by the time spent in the T_g–T_m window via Avrami kinetics, not by polymer grade alone.
